kf: **Pigmented contact dermatitis (Riehl melanosis)**: grey-brown facial and neck pigment with little visible eczema, mostly in **Fitzpatrick IV–VI** skin.
Triggers: fragrances, essential oils, **PPD hair dye**, kumkum/bindi dyes, textile dyes, preservatives.
Related: **lichen planus pigmentosus** (check the hairline for frontal fibrosing alopecia) and **ashy dermatosis**.
Key step: **patch (± photopatch) testing**; stop non-essential cosmetics and fragrance.
Pigment is dermal, so it fades slowly over many months; avoid potent facial steroids.
myths: **"It's melasma"**: grey-blue tones, neck involvement and cosmetic history suggest contact or lichenoid pigmentation.
patho_lead: Low-grade allergy **damages the basal layer** and pigment **drops into the dermis**.

mech.t: Low-dose allergens trigger a T-cell reaction.
Basal keratinocytes and melanocytes are injured (lichenoid/interface dermatitis).
Melanin falls into the dermis and is eaten by melanophages.
mech.cap: Pigment incontinence: lymphocytes damage the basal layer and melanin drops into dermal macrophages, giving a slate-grey tone.

mech.t: Deep pigment looks grey-blue (Tyndall effect) and fades slowly.
